Kinetic sand is a great way to provide sensory input while still working on a multitude of skills.  I love to use cookie cutters in the sand to work on bilateral skills, pressure and and force regulation.  Cutting with sand is a great introduction to snipping and provides additional sensory feedback. Kids who are struggling with writing tend to be more willing to practice writing on different surfaces. Try sand and use a paint brush for smooth lines.  #occupationaltherapy #ot #sensoryactivities #finemotorskills #sensory #schoolbasedot

A machine that goes nowhere — endlessly moving through time. Günther Uecker’s 'Sand Mill' consists of a slowly rotating mechanism that continuously drags through sand, leaving and erasing traces in an endless cycle. Uecker first created a "Sand Mill" in 1965, and the work became part of his wider exploration of movement, time, repetition and impermanence. He has described the 'Sand Mill' as "the grinding of time" — a poetic image for existence gradually passing away. The marks in the sand also connect to his childhood growing up on a farm, where he experienced the cycles of nature, while his encounters with Japan and Zen gardens brought another influence: an apparently still landscape that is nevertheless constantly changing. The Arp Museum in Bahnhof is currently showing a particularly large example from the 'Sand Mill' series (1969/2014). Nothing is created. Nothing is completed. The movement simply continues. . #KineticArt #MinimalArt #Museum #News #ContemporaryArt
